_readme: The gate requires every experiments/<id>/ that carries archived *_results.json to have
(a) an entry in storage/memory/knowledge.json and (b) a valid reproduce_spec.json.
An exclusion is an admission that a finding will stay unrecorded or unreproducible.
It is NEVER the cheap way out of writing an artifact. Every entry must state WHY the
artifact cannot exist -- not that writing it was inconvenient. An entry whose reason is
'will do later' is a bug; write the artifact instead.
Directories with NO archived *_results.json are already outside the gate's scope and do
not belong here -- see the module docstring in scripts/check_experiment_artifacts.py.
The 2026-07-19 sweep found 108 such directories (paper-writing sessions, .gitkeep
placeholders, abandoned stubs); listing them here would be noise, not exemption.
Match is on the leading K-id (e.g. 'k1538' also covers 'k1538_bond_fund_flows') or on

exclusions.reason: Legacy pre-spec run used the gitignored mutable data/cache/price_cache.db without a frozen source snapshot. The exact input vintage no longer exists: the documented TW0050 history revision changed n from 4,263 to 4,264 and prevents exact reconstruction of the archived k1623_results.json. A retroactive reproduce_spec would therefore describe today's database, not the bytes that produced the archived result.

k528_nfp_event_study.py (lines 495-496) fetches SPY and ^VIX daily OHLCV live via yf.download over 2005-01..2026-03 with no committed price snapshot -- data/ holds only the NFP release-calendar fixture (nfp_release_feed_fixture.json). yfinance retroactively revises SPY/VIX history (adjusted-close/split/dividend restatements), so a re-download yields different bytes than the archived k528_nfp_event_study_results.json / k528_nfp_official_dates_results.json. A retroactive reproduce_spec would describe today's yfinance vintage, not the input that produced the archived result -- same unfrozen-live-source class as k1623. The finding itself is recorded (K528 knowledge entry) and Codex primary-path certified PASS @ b2634ed41 on the claim surface; only offline byte-reproduction of the market-data input is impossible.

k1426.py fetch_pair() (lines 53-65) downloads every pair leg live via yf.download with auto_adjust=True and no committed price snapshot; oos.py and oos_return_benchmark.py both import that same loader, so every archived result here (k1426_results.json, k1426_oos_results.json, k1426_oos_return_benchmark.json and the three shards) shares the unfrozen input. auto_adjust restates history on every split and dividend, so a re-download yields different bytes than the archived runs -- same unfrozen-live-source class as k528 and k1623. A retroactive reproduce_spec would pin today's yfinance vintage and claim a reproducibility the archived numbers do not have. The 2026-07-27 change to this directory adds no finding: it persists the daily hedged-return series so the paired return-OLS vs PCH test needs no PCH re-estimation, and corrects the module docstring to state the refit cadence and multistart count the code actually runs.

The 0050.TW 5-min checkpoint chain reads a directory that keeps growing: load_daily_rv() (k1325.py:111) globs data/intraday/0050_TW_5min_*.csv with no upper date bound. The archived k1325_results.json is the 82-day vintage (2026-01-20..2026-06-01); the same glob today returns 123 files, so re-running the script cannot reproduce the archived numbers -- and those numbers are cited publicly in article mile_3445217e. Writing a reproduce_spec now would therefore have to be hand-authored after the fact against an input the script no longer sees, which is exactly the K1708 divergence class volpred.research.reproduce_spec was built to make unrepresentable. The run predates finalize_experiment(), so there is no run-time snapshot to recover. The 2026-08-02 change to this directory adds no finding and touches no estimation path: it deletes the hardcoded REVISIT_GATE_TOTAL_DAYS/REVISIT_GATE_TEST_DAYS constants in favour of volpred.research.revisit_gate, and adds the generated revisit_gate.json. Remove this exclusion when the chain's next checkpoint pins its input glob to an explicit date range and emits its spec via finalize_experiment().

Same unbounded-glob input as k1325: k1324.py loads data/intraday/0050_TW_5min_*.csv with no upper date bound, so the archived 80-day k1324_results.json cannot be reproduced from today's directory (123 files). Its result is also the comparison baseline quoted inside k1325_results.json, so re-running it to synthesise a spec would move a number another archived artifact depends on. Predates finalize_experiment(); no run-time snapshot exists. The 2026-08-02 change removes the two hardcoded revisit thresholds in favour of the shared volpred.research.revisit_gate and adds no finding.

Same unbounded-glob input as k1324/k1325 (data/intraday/0050_TW_5min_*.csv, no upper date bound), archived at the 76-day vintage and quoted forward as the baseline inside k1324_results.json. Predates finalize_experiment(); no run-time snapshot exists, and a hand-written spec would pin today's 123-file directory rather than the input that produced the archived result. The 2026-08-02 change removes the hardcoded REVISIT_GATE_DAYS = 200 constant in favour of the shared volpred.research.revisit_gate and adds no finding.

k1307.py is a sample-readiness diagnostic whose input, data/intraday/0050_TW_daily_rv.csv, is appended to by the daily RV collector -- the file grew from the archived vintage to 123 non-null days by 2026-08-02, so its verdict is a function of when it ran and cannot be byte-reproduced later. Same unfrozen-live-source class as k1623, with the mutation on this side of the repo rather than a vendor's. Predates finalize_experiment(). The 2026-08-02 change removes the hardcoded POWERED_OOS_TARGET = 252 constant -- a second, inconsistent copy of the same pipeline's revisit threshold -- in favour of volpred.research.revisit_gate, and adds no finding.

k994.py (lines 368-392) downloads ^VIX and every asset live via yf.download over DATA_START 2005-01-01 to DATA_END 2026-04-08 with no committed price snapshot, so archived k994_results.json cannot be byte-reproduced offline -- same unfrozen-live-source class as k528 and k1623. This is a KNOWN OPEN GAP, not a settled exemption: task k892_k994_pinned_snapshot_repoint_20260721 exists to repoint this loader at a pinned snapshot, and is blocked because the available 0050.TW snapshot (paper/garch-x-vix/data/0050_tw_vix_2007-2022.csv) ends in 2022 while the paper-cited DM t=1.44 (paper/garch-x-vix/main.tex:531) is an OOS statistic over 2019-01-01..2026-04-08. Repointing at that CSV would truncate the OOS window and silently change a published number. The gap and the decision it needs are written up in experiments/k994/PINNED_REPOINT_COVERAGE_GAP.md -- the only 2026-07-27 change to this directory. Remove this exclusion once a snapshot covers the cited window; the k892 half of the same task is already done and verified.

K1342.py:72 pulls its only input with yf.download(period="60d", interval="2m") -- a ROLLING window, not a pinned date range, against a feed Yahoo only retains for the last 60 days. The window that produced the archived K1342_results.json has therefore expired at the source: it is not merely revised (the k1623 case), it is unobtainable. K1342_daily_signals.csv cannot stand in as a snapshot -- K1342.py:398 WRITES it, so it is output, not input. A reproduce_spec authored now would hash today's 60 days and claim they generated a result they did not, which is the exact K1708 divergence class volpred.research.reproduce_spec exists to make unrepresentable. Remove this exclusion when the next checkpoint in this line commits a frozen snapshot of its 2m bars, or moves to a source that accepts an explicit start/end date.
